summary: Iter_18 photo-upload safety improvements VERIFIED. Backend: 14/14 unit + integration tests passing in /app/backend/tests/test_journal_upload_safety.py (4 skipped due to external Gemini quota 503 saturado — NOT a code failure). The critical assertions all pass: (a) routers.journal._save_photo accepts jpg/jpeg/png/webp/heic/heif with correct filename suffix, (b) unknown extensions fall back to .jpg, (c) empty body → HTTP 400 with detail 'Imagen vacía…', (d) 18 MB body accepted (proving the 12→20 MB cap raise), (e) 22 MB body rejected with HTTP 413 and Spanish detail containing 'MB' + 'máximo' + '20 MB', (f) live end-to-end 15 MB upload passes _save_photo (non-413 response), (g) live 22 MB upload rejected with 413. Frontend: all required markers exist in bundle (_compressImage, ocr-start-file-fallback, ocr-end-file-fallback, _friendlyUploadError, ocrUploadProgress, onUploadProgress, timeout: 90_000, maxContentLength: 25*1024*1024, window.addEventListener('focus'), document.body.appendChild(input)). _compressImage confirmed: short-circuits <900KB, maxSide=1600, JPEG quality 0.85, ctx.fillStyle=#FFFFFF drawn before drawImage, returns File with type='image/jpeg'. Playwright smoke test on preview URL: navigated admin/admin → Gestión → 'Gestión / Salario' page, verified 'Jornada con foto del taxímetro' section renders at top, verified fallback <input> with data-testid='ocr-start-file-fallback' is present with helper text '¿Problemas con la cámara? Sube una foto guardada:', successfully uploaded /tmp/tiny.jpg via setInputFiles → request reached backend → backend returned 503 (Gemini quota saturado) → the friendly Spanish error banner 'El servicio de IA está temporalmente saturado. Espera unos segundos e inténtalo de nuevo.' rendered in the .ocr-error div. This EXACTLY validates _friendlyUploadError formatting + graceful UX. Progress bar and 'Subiendo foto… XX%' text could not be observed live because the 503 came back in <1s; code path verified by grep only.

minor.issue: Ext whitelist forces fallback to 'jpg' when the browser sends 'jfif' (older windows) or 'avif'; not blocking today but consider adding avif/jfif to the allow-list if users report.

External flakiness: Gemini API returned 503 'servicio saturado' during 4 of the live integration attempts. This is a quota/rate issue on the Gemini side, not our code. The error IS handled gracefully (503 with friendly Spanish detail surfacing to the client, no crash).

ui_bugs.issue: data-testid='ocr-start-button' set on TouchableOpacity is NOT propagated to the rendered <div> by react-native-web. DOM inspection showed the parent div has tabindex+cursor classes but no data-testid attribute. Impact: automated tests must locate this button by text (currently works) rather than by data-testid. Same issue likely affects ocr-add-fuel and other TouchableOpacity-based testids. Fix: pass testID as a prop (RN uses testID → RN Web maps it) OR wrap with a View that carries data-testid, OR use dataSet={{ testid: 'ocr-start-button' }} which RN Web maps to data-testid.

integration_issues.issue: Live progress-bar smoke could not be captured because Gemini 503 short-circuits the response in <1s (before axios's onUploadProgress emits an intermediate tick). Code-side verified (ocrUploadProgress state exists, progress bar JSX at line 13314-13318, onUploadProgress at 13359). Recommend a slower/dev-mode test to record the % ticks — cosmetic.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Make TouchableOpacity data-testid propagate to the DOM. Use dataSet={{ testid: 'ocr-start-button' }} or migrate to Pressable, or wrap the button in a <View data-testid>. This blocks future Playwright tests from using stable selectors on the main FOTO button; currently we can only reach it by text.

NOTE (not a code fix): User's production nginx still needs client_max_body_size ≥ 20M for the raised backend cap to be reachable in prod. The compression pipeline (target <1MB after client-side JPEG re-encode) is the main mitigation and should cover >95% of real phone uploads without needing the nginx bump.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers/journal.py:221-245 _save_photo — the 20 MB cap is enforced AFTER file.read() into memory. On very large abusive bodies (>100 MB from an unauthenticated attacker) this could pin RAM. Not a regression from iter_18 (was there before), but worth streaming or using request.stream() and enforcing size incrementally if this ever becomes public-facing.

backend/routers/journal.py:230-232 empty-body check runs AFTER await file.read(). If a large empty-but-not-truly-empty multipart part is sent, the check works, but 'Imagen vacía' message is helpful — good UX.

backend/routers/journal.py:222-227 the ext whitelist correctly downgrades unknown extensions to .jpg (safe default) — this matches the front-end which always sends compressed .jpg after _compressImage.

frontend/app/index.tsx:491-539 _compressImage — well-written: short-circuits <900 KB, applies maxSide=1600 with correct aspect ratio, uses quality 0.85, paints a white background BEFORE drawImage to avoid black-on-transparent artifacts for PNGs/HEICs with alpha. Correctly returns File with type='image/jpeg' and .jpg extension via filename.replace. Revokes ObjectURL on both success and error paths.

frontend/app/index.tsx:541-585 ocrPickFile — solid: attaches the input to document.body BEFORE .click() (mobile-safari fix), uses window focus listener as a fallback resolution path (bypass unreliable oncancel), removes both the DOM node and the focus listener on finish. resolved boolean prevents double-resolution.

frontend/app/index.tsx:641-681 ocrStartShift — good UX: axios timeout 90_000 (long enough for Gemini + retries), maxContentLength+maxBodyLength 25 MB (headroom above the backend 20 MB cap), onUploadProgress updates state cleanly. _friendlyUploadError branches on axios error shape and returns Spanish user-friendly text.

frontend/app/index.tsx:13340-13376 fallback plain input — critically correct: does NOT wrap the native <input> in a TouchableOpacity, so it keeps its data-testid AND its native file-picker behavior. Style is dim (#94A3B8) with clear helper text, positioned below the main button. Good redundancy for the mobile-camera-failure case that the user reported.

frontend/app/index.tsx main FOTO button (13325-13333) — data-testid='ocr-start-button' is set on TouchableOpacity but not propagated to DOM by react-native-web. Test selectors must fall back to text-based lookup. Not a bug in the upload path, but a testability gap.

GENERAL: the entire upload safety path is idempotent — every function short-circuits on error and never leaves the UI in a busy state (finally blocks reset ocrBusy and ocrUploadProgress). Great defense in depth.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Primary regression: /app/backend/tests/test_journal_upload_safety.py — 18 tests covering the _save_photo unit (extensions, 20 MB cap, empty-body handling, size boundaries) and the live upload cycle including 15 MB and 22 MB body limits. The 4 TestLiveJournalCycle tests use Gemini and will pytest.skip() when quota is exhausted (503 'servicio saturado'), which happened during iter_18 run — this is expected behavior. Skip logic recognizes 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED', '429', 'SATURADO', 'INTERNAL SERVER ERROR'. The 22 MB test is critical and always runs (no Gemini call needed — 413 fires before OCR). Frontend smoke was done with Playwright against the preview URL: login flow uses 3 <input>s (destino, username, password) so use get_by_placeholder('Nombre de usuario') and input[type='password'] selectors to avoid accidentally filling the tariff-calc DESTINO field. Navigate to Gestión by clicking the id^='page-selector-' dropdown then get_by_text('Gestión', exact=True). Note: TouchableOpacity 'FOTO INICIO DE JORNADA' does NOT expose data-testid to the DOM — locate by text only. The fallback input 'ocr-start-file-fallback' is a native <input type=file> and DOES expose the data-testid (RN Web preserves data-* on raw HTML tags).
rca_of_the_issue: USER BUG: 'no e sido capaz de subir una fotografia' — user could not upload a taximeter photo in production because (a) phone cameras generate 3-10 MB JPEGs but nginx client_max_body_size defaults to 1 MB → 413 silent fail; (b) `oncancel` on hidden <input type=file> is not reliable → promise never resolved → button hung; (c) no client-side compression → payload too big; (d) no progress indicator so user thought the app froze; (e) no friendly Spanish error → user gave up. Iter_18 fix, VERIFIED by this test suite: (1) backend _save_photo cap raised 12 → 20 MB with a Spanish 'La imagen ocupa X MB y el máximo son 20 MB' message on the 413, and the ext whitelist now accepts HEIC/HEIF for iPhone; (2) ocrPickFile attaches the <input> to document.body before .click() (mobile-safari bug), uses window.focus listener as a resolution fallback for the unreliable oncancel, and pipes through _compressImage which downsizes to 1600px longest side at JPEG quality 0.85 — most real phone photos come out at ~200-800 KB; (3) axios call has timeout: 90_000 + maxContentLength: 25 MB + onUploadProgress that updates a live percentage state driving a green progress bar; (4) errors go through _friendlyUploadError producing Spanish messages like 'El servicio de IA está temporalmente saturado…' (LIVE-verified in the Playwright smoke — Gemini was actually saturado during the run and the banner appeared correctly); (5) a fallback plain <input type=file> is rendered directly below the main FOTO button so users on desktop or with camera issues can pick a saved photo. Bug is functionally resolved on the client + server side. User still needs a one-line nginx tweak in production to enable the full 20 MB headroom, but the compression pipeline makes that virtually unnecessary.
